name: Sorge, eq. (36): int_V sqrt(-g) T^i_(C) i = 0 for a complete Casimir apparatus

source.located: F. Sorge, 'Quasi-local Casimir energy and vacuum buoyancy in a weak gravitational field', arXiv:2011.10991v1 [gr-qc], 22 Nov 2020 (INFN Napoli); eqs (29)-(40), sec. 6; appendix eqs (64)-(72)
source.via: alphaXiv get_paper_content(fullText=true) -- whole paper read, 20 pp. incl. references. Only v1 was read; the acknowledgment thanks referees, so a journal version exists (not read; the tree's precedent: discrepancies below are NOT to be quoted against the journal version until it is read).

published_statement: Sec. 6, from the equilibrium equation f_nu + nabla_mu T^mu_(C) nu = 0 (31) in the Fermi metric ds^2 = (1+2 gamma z)dt^2 - dx^2 - dy^2 - dz^2 (30), with the weight identified as F_z = int_V d^3x sqrt(-g) f_z = m gamma = gamma int_V d^3x sqrt(-g)[T^t_t - T^i_i]_(C) (32): 'The first and the last term cancel each other [at the O(gamma) order ...]' (34)->(35); 'The last term is zero, since it can be converted to a surface integral on the boundary dV of the cavity volume, where T^mu nu_(C) = 0. The second term is zero, as the cavity does not exchange energy and momentum with the surroundings. As a consequence int_V d^3x sqrt(-g) T^i_(C) i = 0. (36)'. Then m = int_V sqrt(-g) T^t_(C) t (37), T_(C) = T_(phi) + T_(cav) (38). p.11: 'it appears evident the cancellation between the space-like components of the stress-energy tensors T_(phi) and T_(cav) ... We point out that such cancellation basically relies on the virial theorem [2]'. Boxed conclusion p.11: 'We have thus proved that if (according to the Equivalence Principle) the gravitational and inertial (quasi-local Tolman) mass associated to the field quantum vacuum coincide, then the quasi-local mass value is related solely to the T^t_(phi) t component'. Abstract: 'it is possible to attribute a Tolman mass to a massless scalar field confined to a Casimir cavity'.
published_hypotheses: H1 weak static field, first order in gamma only: Fermi metric (30) 'To first order, and neglecting rotations', O(|x|^2) dropped; gamma uniform over the apparatus (sec. 5)
H2 the apparatus is a test system: T_(C) does not appreciably influence the background (assumption (c), sec. 3; sqrt(-g_T) ~ sqrt(-g), eq. (27))
H3 compact support: T^mu nu_(C) = 0 outside and on the boundary dV of the integration volume (assumption (a); eq. (29) 'T^mu nu_(C) = 0 outside the cavity'; used to kill int d_j T^j_z in (35))
H4 stationarity: int d_t T^t_z = 0 ('the cavity does not exchange energy and momentum with the surroundings'; footnote 1, the field fluctuations are fast compared with lab times)
H5 held at rest by an external non-gravitational force density f_nu (31) -- a NON-closed system

H6 THE PREMISE (32): the weight equals gamma times the quasi-local Tolman mass (29), justified by the Equivalence Principle -- eq. (36) is derived FROM it; the paper says the result 'basically relies on the Equivalence Principle, which was indeed employed in deriving the result (40)'
H7 complete apparatus: T_(C) = T_(phi) + T_(cav) (38); T_(cav) is never modelled -- the field/wall cancellation is inferred from the integral, not computed

H8 model: massless minimally coupled scalar field, Dirichlet parallel plates, L << sqrt(A_perp), edge effects neglected (sec. 2); the paper notes different fields give different Tolman masses (p.11) -- eq. (36) itself does not use the field's form
H9 the cancellation is attributed (not proved independently) to the virial theorem, citing Landau-Lifshitz [2], Carlip [55], Ohanian [10]
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (premise), tolman.py:167-169 'proves int_V sqrt(-g) T^i_(C) i = 0 for the apparatus (his eq. 36)': Sorge derives (36) from conservation PLUS the premise (32) F_z = gamma m_Tolman (H6); his own boxed statement is conditional ('if ... coincide, then ...'). Re-derived here (C): conservation ALONE gives F_z = gamma int sqrt(-g) T^tt (Calloni's result); adding (32) gives EXACTLY int sqrt(-g) T^i_i = 2 gamma int sqrt(-g) z T^tt. The conclusion does not fall: flat-space von Laue (static, divergence-free, compactly supported T^ij => int T^ij = 0) supplies it independently at O(gamma^0), machine-checked in D. So 'proves' overstates Sorge's logic; the content is carried by von Laue, which tolman.py already cites through Wang 1206.5618 eq. (20).

DROPPED (order), tolman.py:171-172 '4 pi R^3 p_r(R) = 0 identically' and tolman.py:2608-2609 'returns exactly zero': (36) enters (35) multiplied by gamma, so it is established only at O(gamma^0); the O(gamma) remainder 2 gamma int z T^tt depends on the origin of z (frame-dependent) and, physically, on HOW the apparatus is held (E: a column hung vs supported gives int T^zz = +/- gamma M h/2). Relative size gamma h/c^2 = 1.1e-22 (1 um), 1.1e-18 (1 cm), 1.1e-16 (1 m). In the tree's own setting (a fixed, unsourced background, flat for the plate cell; HYPOTHESES 'test_field_background') von Laue is exact and 'identically' is correct; the drift is in citing a weak-field O(gamma) paper for an exact zero. No conclusion moves.

WEAKENED (what 'complete' means), tolman.py:170-171 'for a COMPLETE apparatus -- field plus mirrors': field plus mirrors is not a static closed system -- the Casimir attraction must be carried by whatever holds the plates apart. Sorge's T_(cav) (H7) is 'the cavity itself', never modelled; Fulling et al. hep-th/0702091 p.3 (READ): 'the energy-momentum tensor of the complete physical situation must be conserved ... if we included a physical mechanism holding the plates apart against the Casimir attraction'. Checked (D): the EM field alone has int sum_i T^ii = E_total != 0 (Tolman mass 2E), so the spacers/frame must carry -E_total. Naming gap in the tree's gloss; the refusal is unaffected.

WIDENED (the refusal's stated ground), tolman.py:173-174 'REFUSES on a ball containing a mirror', :549 'any ball enclosing a mirror : REFUSE (Sorge eq. 36, section 1)', :1016-1017, :2974 'a ball enclosing a mirror: REFUSE (von Laue, Sorge eq. 36)': eq. (36) and von Laue cover only a region containing the WHOLE support (H3). A ball that contains one mirror but cuts the apparatus is not covered: there int T^i_i is generally NONZERO (D: sub-ball -27 pi/8; partial-frame strip -24/35; interior strip -2097152/688905). The refusal is still correct -- the test has no licensed content where unmodelled wall stress enters -- but for a cutting ball its ground is 'unmodelled wall stress', not 'integrates to zero'. A refusal is a non-claim, so this is not over-representation in either direction; it is a mis-cited ground.

ADDED (field transfer), tolman.py:2607-2609 (switch.py, 'the EM switch') applies the scalar-field paper to an EM apparatus: harmless -- the derivation of (36) uses only conservation, compact support, stationarity and (32), not the scalar Lagrangian; Fulling et al. make the same complete-conservation point for the EM plates.

PARAPHRASE, tolman.py:167-168 'attributes a Tolman mass to a Casimir cavity': the abstract says 'to a massless scalar field confined to a Casimir cavity'. Minor; the quotation 'basically relies on the virial theorem' (tolman.py:169-170) is verbatim (p.11).

SOURCE-SIDE DISCREPANCY, not the tree's: Sorge eq. (33) prints (1/sqrt(-g)) d_mu T^mu_(C) z where the covariant divergence is (1/sqrt(-g)) d_mu(sqrt(-g) T^mu_z) - Gamma-term. Checked (C): the difference after the measure is d_j((sqrt(-g)-1) T^j_z), itself a total derivative, so it does not reach (36). Recorded as a display discrepancy in v1, not an error; the journal version was not read.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What Sorge had (2020): the Casimir stress for the scalar field, the Fermi metric to O(gamma), the Calloni/Fulling/Bimonte results, and NO measurement of vacuum weight (Archimedes still at pathfinder stage). What came later: nothing located that measures the Casimir-apparatus weight. Does the missing datum change the conclusion? NO, evidence: eq. (36) is not an empirical claim -- sec. C shows it is algebraically equivalent (given conservation) to the premise F_z = gamma m_Tolman, and sec. D shows it is independently forced at O(gamma^0) by flat-space von Laue for any static, conserved, compactly supported stress. A vacuum-weight measurement would test the EP premise (H6) and Calloni's F_z = gamma E, not the identity. What the paper does lack is not data but MODELLING: T_(cav) is never written, so the field/wall cancellation is inferred, not shown; that gap is closed here generically (D), not for a specific wall model. M's hypothesis is therefore not supported for this result; the limitations found are hypotheses (order in gamma, completeness of the apparatus, the EP premise), all now named.
grade_evidence: Read at source (v1, full text). The identity holds -- re-derived from the conservation law in metric (30) and independently by von Laue (27/27 sympy checks) -- but on a smaller class than the tree's wording: (i) Sorge's (36) is derived from the EP premise (32) and is established at O(gamma^0) only (exact remainder 2 gamma int sqrt(-g) z T^tt, support-dependent), whereas tolman.py:167-172 says 'proves' and 'identically'; (ii) 'complete apparatus' must include the struts that hold the plates apart, not just 'field plus mirrors' (tolman.py:170-171; EM field alone gives int sum T^ii = E_total != 0); (iii) the identity covers only regions containing the WHOLE support, while the refusal is keyed to 'a ball containing a mirror' (tolman.py:173-174, :549, :2974), where int T^i_i is shown nonzero. Nothing resting on it moves: the `ball_excludes_walls` refusal is a non-claim and stays correct (its ground for a cutting ball is unmodelled wall stress, not a zero); PEER_STATUS 'own reach NARROWED' is if anything reinforced; the switch.py caution holds in the flat test-field setting where von Laue is exact. Not WRONG: no counterexample to (36) within its hypotheses; the eq. (33) display is a discrepancy that does not propagate. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: no datum enters (36).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: reword tolman.py's gloss to 'von Laue (flat, exact) -- Sorge eq. (36) is its O(gamma^0) weak-field restatement under the EP premise (32); complete = field + mirrors + whatever holds them apart; zero only on a ball enclosing the whole support' (a human seats any change). To WRONG: a static, conserved, compactly supported apparatus with int T^i_i != 0 at O(gamma^0) -- none exists (von Laue, sec. D). To OPEN/other: the journal version of 2011.10991 differing materially from v1 in eqs (32)-(36) (not read here).
